_comment: Fixtures for the OKF consumption test. See
Every 'grounding' string is copied verbatim from the compiled wiki. If a
case starts failing on 'grounded', check whether the compile changed the
wording before assuming the agent is at fault.
Cases favour rulings a model cannot derive from general knowledge, several
of which invert the usual convention. That is what lets this test fail when
the agent answers from priors instead of reading the wiki.
expect_present - every string must appear in the rewrite
expect_absent  - no string may appear in the rewrite
expect_any     - at least one string must appear (open-ended fixes)

cases.input: Revenues rose 12 per cent last year, and the board expects a further 4 per cent in 2026.
cases.grounding: Use the sign % instead of per cent
cases.note: Inverts the common convention: most guides spell it out, this one requires the sign.

cases.input: The new tariff impacted margins across the region.
cases.note: House prohibition on verbing nouns; any valid replacement passes.

cases.input: The launch was delayed due to a shortage of chips.
cases.note: Adverbial 'due to' is the disputed usage.

cases.input: The frost decimated the entire orchard, leaving not a single tree alive.
cases.note: The paragraph describes total destruction, which the ruling reserves other words for.

cases.input: Less than seven firms bid for the contract.
cases.grounding: Use fewer, not less, with individual items

cases.input: Hopefully, the merger will close before the end of the quarter.
cases.note: The wiki concedes this is not grammatically wrong and forbids it anyway - unguessable from priors.

cases.input: The airline's alibi for the delay, a shortage of crew, convinced nobody.
cases.grounding: not the same thing as a false explanation
cases.note: An alibi is being elsewhere, not an excuse.

cases.input: Compared to last year, profits fell sharply while costs climbed.
cases.grounding: compared with is used to evaluate similarities
cases.note: The sentence evaluates and highlights differences, so 'with'.
